record.paper_title: Open Problems in Hydrodynamical Approach to Relativistic Heavy Ion Collisions
record.original_question: How can relativistic hydrodynamics for nuclear collisions be extended to include finite-size corrections when the microscopic mean-free path or correlation length λ_micro is not negligible compared with the hydrodynamical inhomogeneity scale λ_Hydro, so that the expansion parameter x = λ_micro/λ_Hydro is not much smaller than one, especially for determining local energy density and QCD phase-transition properties?

evidence.quote: Strictly speaking, the hydrodynamics is essentially the zero mean-free path (or correlation length) approximation for the microscopic degrees of freedom compared to the system size. For the nuclear collisions, this is not a trivial approximation.

The parameter which characterizes the degree of approximation with respect to the finite size of the system would be x = λmicro/λHydro where λmicro is the typical mean-free path (or the correlation length) of the constituent particles and λHydro is the hydrodynamical inhomogeneity scale.
Hydrodynamics is valid for x ≪ 1, so that when the local inhomogeneity scale in the system is of the order of the mean-free path, the hydrodynamics should break down.

In any case, the finite size effect on the local energy density is an important question, in particular with respect to the properties of phase transition. A further investigation on this direction is now in progress.

artifact.status_search_result: The problem of extending relativistic hydrodynamics into the finite Knudsen-number regime (x = λ_micro/λ_Hydro not small) remains an active research area. Recent work develops second-order and resummed viscous hydrodynamics, hydrodynamic attractors, and Knudsen-based classifications of collectivity, but no complete, universally accepted framework controls finite-size corrections to local energy density and phase-transition observables. The question is therefore still open, with substantial partial progress.

status_evidence.title: Applicability of Hydrodynamics in the Hadronic Phase of Heavy-Ion Collisions
status_evidence.snippet: The Knudsen number indicates applicability of hydrodynamics; when it reaches a critical value, hydrodynamics breaks down.
status_evidence.claim: Hydrodynamic validity is still actively assessed via the Knudsen number, indicating ongoing investigation.

status_evidence.title: Knudsen number and universal behavior of collective flows
status_evidence.snippet: The Knudsen number provides a unified criterion for classifying collectivity across systems including small systems where thermalisation may not be fully realised.
status_evidence.claim: Finite-Knudsen-number behavior of collective flow is still being characterized in 2025.

status_evidence.title: Hydrodynamics from free-streaming to thermalization and back again
status_evidence.snippet: Trajectory of Reynolds vs Knudsen number characterizes the transition from thermalizing to decoupling dynamics.
status_evidence.claim: Bridging hydrodynamics and finite-mean-free-path regimes remains a topic of current research.

status_evidence.title: Relativistic Hydrodynamics in Heavy-Ion Collisions: General Aspects and Recent Developments
status_evidence.snippet: Review of viscous and higher-order relativistic hydrodynamics developments.
status_evidence.claim: Reviews document partial progress through dissipative and second-order formulations but no closed-form solution for finite x.
